chapter_theme: Chariyai (சரியை), the first of the four Saiva paths: seeking out temples and towns, singing and bowing to Siva until he takes the heart as his temple. The chapter sets chariyai in the ladder of chariyai, kiriyai, yoga and jnana, matches each to a kind of worship and a kind of devotee, and ends with the four grades of initiation.
structure_note: An opening that names the teachers of the root chariyai (1443), a verse ranking four kinds of puja (1444), the one verse on chariyai practice itself (1445), two verses matching the four paths to four kinds of people (1446, 1447), worship by form and formless (1448), Nandi's giving of the paths (1449) and the four initiations (1450). The same fourfold scheme of samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka closes chapters 93 and 94.

1443.reading: This is the way of the root chariyai, as Kalangi, Kanjamalaiyan and Kandhuru examined it; listen: on earth it is the life of pure Saivam.
1443.nuance: காலாங்கி, கஞ்சமலையமான் and கந்துரு are taken as disciples of Tirumular named in the lineage verses; the readings of the names, especially கந்துரு, are not secure. மூல சரியை may mean the root or first chariyai, or the chariyai of Mulan.

1444.reading: Standing as the life of life is the bright jnana-puja; looking at the light in the life is the great yoga-puja; invoking the deity into a form is outer puja; love at the end of all fault is Siva-puja.
1444.nuance: ஆவாகனம் is the ritual invocation of the deity into an image, the work of kiriyai. செயிற்கடை நேசம் (love at the end of fault, or love free of fault) is obscure; it is usually taken as the devotee's pure love, the puja of chariyai. The verse ranks inner over outer worship without dismissing the outer.

1445.reading: Seek through lands, towns and holy temples, and sing 'Siva Peruman'; having sung, bow; and when you have bowed, he will take your joined heart as his temple.
1445.nuance: The outward wandering of chariyai ends inward: the temple sought outside becomes the heart. கூடிய நெஞ்சம் may be the heart that has come together in devotion, or the heart joined to him.

1446.reading: The devotees are those in chariyai; those of kiriyai are servants who take the garb of grace; the practisers of pure yama and the rest are pure yogis; the siddhas are those who go and reach Siva-jnana.
1446.nuance: The verse matches the four paths to four kinds of people: பத்தர், தொண்டர், யோகர், சித்தர். வியமாதி is read as இயமாதி (yama and the other limbs); அருள்வேடம் (the garb of grace) may be holy ash and rudraksha or the guise of devotees.

1447.reading: Those of true jnana who have become Him, those of the eightfold yoga, the siddhas in samadhi, those of kiriyai who never fail in archana, and those of chariyai: all are of this wide earth.
1447.nuance: The list runs down from jnana to chariyai, the reverse of 1446. வெண் யோகம் is read as எண் யோகம், eight-limbed yoga. நீள்நிலத்தோர் (those of the wide earth) may honour all four as living on earth, or may mark them all as still within the world.

1448.reading: Kiriyai, the yogas and the rising jnana-puja; the rare form of Siva and the formless in which he dwells; the puja chosen at the stage when one can discern: these are the high puja of love.
1448.nuance: Tradition matches kiriyai to worship of Siva in form (உரு), yoga to form-and-formless, and jnana to the formless (அரூபம்); the verse names form and formless but doesn't spell out the match. தெரியும் பருவம் (the stage of discerning) suggests worship fitted to one's ripeness.

1449.reading: The four paths beginning with chariyai, the four jnanas they give, and the six of wide Vedanta and Siddhanta: Nandi, who is their meaning, came to the golden city and set them for deluded men to worship.
1449.nuance: தருஞான நான்கும் is taken as the four fruits of the paths, or the fourfold division of each path. ஆறும் (the six) is unclear: six schools, or six divisions of Vedanta-Siddhanta. பொன்னகர் (the golden city) may be Tillai, Kailasa or the world. Nandi is both teacher and the meaning taught.

1450.reading: Samaya initiation is purity of many kinds in which one's own action ceases; visesha is purification by Hara's mantra; nirvana is purification of the kalas; abhisheka is the path of settled jnana.
1450.nuance: சமயம், விசேடம், நிருவாணம் and அபிடேகம் are the four grades of Saiva initiation (தீட்சை) in the Agamas, though the verse does not use the word தீட்சை. Here சமயம் is the first initiation, not a sect. கலாசுத்தி, the purifying of the kalas, is a technical rite.

links.note: 1445 ends the pilgrim's search with the Lord taking the heart as his temple; 1823 builds the whole temple inside: heart as shrine, body as temple, mouth as gate, the soul as linga.
Both make Nandi the giver of the paths: in 1449 he sets the four paths for deluded men, in 1478 he lays down the guru-path so that those on earth may be saved.

1443 names Kalangi, Kanjamalaiyan and Kandhuru as those who examined the root chariyai (காலாங்கி கஞ்சமலையமான் ... கந்துரு). 69 names the same three (கந்துருக் காலாங்கி கஞ்ச மலையனோடு) among the seven of Tirumular's line who received the mantra. The pair shows the disciples of the preface's lineage also cited as authorities for the paths.

1443 calls chariyai the life of pure Saivam on earth (சுத்த சைவத்து உயிரதே). The Thiruppugazh song asks when the poet, leaving the base trade of praise songs for patrons, will live doing chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை கிரியைசெய்து உயிர்வாழ்வேன்). Both make chariyai what one lives by, in Tirumular as doctrine and in Arunagirinathar as a hope.

1444 ranks the pujas: standing as the life of life is jnana-puja, invoking the deity into a form (ஆவாகனம்) is outer puja. 1607 gives an inner puja in the same terms: seeing self and He within and offering the flower called 'self' at His feet (தானென்ற பூவை அவனடி சாத்தினால்). 1607 shows what the inner worship 1444 ranks highest looks like as an act.

2614 says he is not in the temple, not in the garb (கோயிலுள் ளானலன் ... வேடத்துள் ளானலன்), but in the hidden heart of those who gave up longing. 1445 tells one to seek through lands, towns and temples (நற்றிருக் கோயிலும் தேடித் திரிந்து), sing and bow, and then he takes the heart as his temple (நெஞ்சத்துக் கோயிலாய்க் கொள்வனே). 1445 qualifies 2614's denial: the temple is not where he stays, but seeking it is the road to the heart where he does.

1445 tells one to wander searching (தேடித் திரிந்து) through towns and temples and sing (பாடுமின்) 'Siva Peruman'. The Thiruppugazh song asks to stop wandering, singing (பாடிப் பாடி) crores of Tamil garlands and searching (தேடித் தேடி) for the doors of fools. The same searching and singing is the chariyai of the Saiva in one and the poet's begging trade in the other; the object, the Lord or the patron, decides its worth.

1447 names those of jnana who have become Him, the yogis, the kiriyai people who never fail in archana and the chariyai people, and calls them all of the wide earth (நீள்நிலத்தோரே). The Thiruppugazh song says the One is hard to speak of for any who have joined chariyai and kiriyai (சரியை க்ரியையும் புணர்ந்தவர் எவராலும் ஓத அரிய) and is seen by those with ample Siva-jnana. The song supports the reading of 1447 that ranks the four, with only the jnanis reaching beyond.

1448 sets kiriyai, the yogas and jnana-puja beside Siva's form (சிவனுரு) and the formless (அரூபம்), chosen by the worshipper's stage. The Thiruppugazh song asks whether Murugan's form is the sum of Veda, chariyai, yoga, kiriyai and jnana, the form with parts (சகளம்), the support-less, or the formless (நிராகார வடிவேயோ). Both pair the four paths with form and formless, Tirumular as graded worship and Arunagirinathar as an open question about the god's form.

source_issues: 1443: the teachers' names (காலாங்கி, கஞ்ச மலையமான், கந்துரு) are divided differently in different readings; கந்துரு is uncertain.
1446: வியமாதி is probably a scribal form of இயமாதி.
1447: வெண் யோகத்தர் probably stands for எண்யோகத்தர் (eight-limbed yoga) after the preceding சேர்ந்த.
